tip.importClipboard:
Add from the clipboard
Copy a server link, a subscription URL, another app's import link or a WireGuard config, then press this.

The text is sorted automatically: subscription addresses become subscriptions, everything else becomes servers.
tip.importFile:
Add from a file
A .txt with links or subscription URLs, a WireGuard .conf, or an Xray JSON config.

The file is sorted the same way as the clipboard: subscriptions and servers separately.
tip.qrFile:
Add from a QR image
Pick a picture or screenshot with a QR code of a server or subscription.
tip.qrClipboard:
Add from a QR in the clipboard
Copy a picture with a QR code (for example, Win+Shift+S over it), then press this.
tip.qrWebcam:
Scan a QR with the webcam
Show the QR code (for example, on your phone screen) to the camera; it's read automatically.
tip.subscriptionAdd:
Add servers and subscriptions
Any way from this menu — clipboard, file, QR, typed in; the program sorts out what it got.

Accepted subscriptions for:
• Happ, Incy — incl. Xray JSON, title, traffic, expiry, auto-update
• v2rayN / v2rayNG, Hiddify, Streisand, v2RayTun, Throne (Nekoray) — base64 or plain list of links

Links: https://…, happ://add/…, throne://subscribe?url=…, sing-box://import-remote-profile?url=…, clash://install-config?url=…, hiddify://import/…
Protocols: VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, Hysteria2, SOCKS

Not supported: happ://crypt… (encrypted), Clash YAML and sing-box JSON configs, TUIC / AmneziaWG servers.
If the list shows an "App not supported" stub, the provider serves only its own app — select the subscription in the panel and press “Rename” to set that app's User-Agent.
tip.inGroup:
Include in auto-switch
Marked servers form the group the auto-switch picks the fastest working one from.

Works when “Auto-switch between marked servers” is on and at least two are marked.
tip.apps:
Per-app routing
Choose programs that always go through the VPN or always directly, whatever the other rules say.
tip.insecure:
Certificate check is off
This server's settings turn off TLS certificate validation (allowInsecure).

Traffic can be intercepted by a fake server. Ask the provider for a link without it.
tip.updates:
Program updates
Checked in the background; turns green and blinks when a new version is out. Click to check now or install.

The update downloads from GitHub only after you confirm, its signature is verified, and the program restarts by itself.
routing.title: Routing
tip.directDomains:
Direct domains
Sites that always open without the VPN, even if the geo rules would send them through it. Example: yandex.ru.

They also resolve through your local DNS, so you get the addresses meant for your region.
domains.title: Direct domains
domains.hint: Type a domain and press comma or Enter to add it as a tag. Traffic to these domains (and their subdomains) bypasses the VPN. Example: yandex.ru covers mail.yandex.ru, disk.yandex.ru.
tip.proxyDomains:
Through-VPN domains
The opposite of direct domains: sites that always go through the VPN, above the geo and direct rules.

Useful when a foreign site is mistakenly counted as Russian and opens directly.
proxyDomains.title: Via-VPN domains
proxyDomains.hint: Type a domain and press comma or Enter to add it as a tag. Traffic to these domains (and their subdomains) goes through the VPN, overriding the direct / Russian-site rules.
dns.title: DNS resolver
dns.hint: Used for traffic that bypasses the VPN. Which one is fastest depends on where you are — check and pick.
dns.noneReachable: No DNS resolver responded — check your connection
tip.dnsCheck:
Check resolvers
Measures how fast each DNS resolver answers from this computer, so you can pick the fastest.
footer.language:

tip.ping:
Quick ping
Shows whether the server's port answers, and how fast — directly from this computer, without the VPN.

A TCP connection is opened to the server's address and port and timed; the list is sorted by that time. It doesn't prove the VPN works through the server, and UDP protocols (WireGuard, Hysteria2) can't be checked this way — use “Ping via server” for that.
rename.title: Rename
routing.killSwitch: Kill-switch (block traffic when tunnel is down)
tip.killSwitch:
Kill-switch
While connected, nothing can leave the computer outside the VPN — including the moments when the tunnel drops.

Windows Firewall (WFP) rules block all traffic except the tunnel, the VPN core itself and the local network. If the connection can't be restored, reconnect to get internet back.
status.killSwitchFail: Connected, but the kill-switch could not be enabled: {0}
tip.autoConnect:
Connect at startup
When SimpleRay starts, it connects right away: to the auto-switch group if it's set up, otherwise to the selected server.
tip.enableIpv6:
IPv6
Off by default: in networks without working IPv6, direct IPv6 connections fail and sites can break.

Turn it on only if your internet provider gives you working IPv6.

Subscriptions panel

tip.renameAny:
Rename
Acts on the list you clicked last: a server gets a new name; a subscription gets a new name and User-Agent.

User-Agent is how the program introduces itself to the provider; some providers send servers only to their own app.
tip.removeAny:
Remove
Acts on the list you clicked last: removes the selected server, or the selected subscription together with all its servers (asks first).
tip.refreshSelected:
Refresh subscriptions
Downloads the current server list from the provider: for the subscription selected in the panel, or for all of them when “All servers” is selected.

Subscriptions also refresh by themselves on the interval the provider sets (once a day by default). The program itself updates separately — see “Updates” at the bottom of the window.
tip.pingProxy:
Ping via server — does the VPN really work?
For each server on screen, checks that traffic actually passes through it and how long a request takes. Shown as the second figure: green ms means it works, red means it doesn't.

How: the program briefly starts its own copy of the VPN core (sing-box) on this computer only — reachable just from 127.0.0.1 and protected by a one-time password. Through each server it opens the same test page the auto-switch uses (generate_204) and times the answer. Then the copy is stopped and its temporary settings file deleted. It works without connecting, also checks UDP protocols, and doesn't touch the current connection.
status.proxyPingNoCore: sing-box not found: the check through servers needs the core folder next to SimpleRay.exe
tip.speedTest:
Speed through the server
Measures how fast the selected server downloads; the result stays next to it as “↓ Mbit/s”.

How: up to 10 MB (no longer than 10 s) is downloaded from speed.cloudflare.com through the same temporary local copy of the VPN core as in “Ping via server”. It spends subscription traffic, so it runs only when you press it.
status.speedTesting: Measuring speed through “{0}” (up to 10 MB / 10 s)…
status.speedFail: Couldn't measure speed through “{0}”: the server didn't pass the download
group.hintOff: Auto-switch is off: the connection goes through the selected server
tray.hintText: The window is hidden here, in the tray. Double-click the icon to open it; right-click → Exit to quit.
tip.about:
About SimpleRay
Version, license (GPL-3.0) and a link to the source code.
tip.connect:
Connect / Disconnect
Turns the VPN on for the whole computer: to the auto-switch group if it's set up, otherwise to the selected server.

A virtual network adapter (TUN) is created and traffic is routed by the rules below. Windows asks for administrator rights the first time.
tip.mode:
Routing mode
• Global — all traffic goes through the VPN.
• Rules — split: what's marked below as direct bypasses the VPN, everything else goes through it.
• Direct — no VPN at all (the program stays ready).
tip.blockAds:
Block ads and trackers
Known ad and tracking domains are blocked for all apps, using the geosite-category-ads-all list.
tip.directRuSites:
Russian sites directly
Sites from the geosite-category-ru list (ya.ru, vk.com, banks, government services…) open without the VPN — fast, and with your real region.
tip.directRuIp:
Russian IPs directly
Connections to addresses that belong to Russia (geoip-ru list) bypass the VPN — covers services the site list doesn't know.
tip.directLan:
Local network directly
Printers, NAS, the router and other devices at home or in the office stay reachable while the VPN is on.
tip.dnsProvider:
DNS for direct traffic
Which resolver turns site names into addresses for traffic that bypasses the VPN. Sites going through the VPN are resolved through the VPN.
tip.autoSwitch:
Auto-switch
On: the connection uses the servers marked “in group” and moves to the fastest working one by itself. Off: only the selected server is used.

How: every 3 minutes the VPN core opens a test page through each marked server and measures the time; it switches when another server is faster by more than 50 ms or the current one stops answering.
tip.importManual:
Type or paste
Enter a server link, a subscription URL or another app's import link by hand; it's sorted the same way as the clipboard.
